abstract: >-
  **Summary:** Whole-genome sequencing of *Mycobacterium tuberculosis* serves two analytical tiers in practice — routine per-sample lineage and drug-resistance profiling, and cohort-level joint-genotyping with structural-variant detection for transmission and research studies — but these are served by separate tools with incompatible input formats, forcing laboratories to maintain two pipelines and two samplesheets for the same isolates. We present tbanalyzer, an nf-core pipeline that drives both tiers from a single samplesheet: `--mode mtbseq` runs per-sample profiling and `--mode magma` runs cohort joint-genotyping with structural-variant calling, with shared quality-control and reporting across both. # 1. Introduction

*M. tuberculosis* whole-genome sequencing is used at two analytical tiers. Routine surveillance runs each isolate through per-sample lineage classification and drug-resistance prediction — the workload of MTBseq [@kohl2018mtbseq] and TB-Profiler [@phelan2019tbprofiler]. Research and transmission studies additionally require cohort-level *joint* genotyping and structural-variant detection — the workload of MAGMA [@heupink2023magma]. In current practice these tiers are served by different tools with **incompatible samplesheets and codebases**, so a laboratory that wants to re-analyse a routine cohort at research depth must reformat its inputs, stand up a second pipeline, and retrain staff. No prior tool unifies the two paradigms behind one input format.

> **The contribution — the warrant.** Since a single nf-core pipeline that drives both per-sample resistance profiling and cohort-level joint-genotyping-with-SV from *one* samplesheet removes the dual-pipeline overhead of maintaining separate input formats and codebases for the same isolates, a surveillance laboratory can re-run a cohort at research depth without reformatting inputs or retraining staff. The contribution is this **mode-switching abstraction** — an interface-design decision with operational consequences — not the underlying callers, which are wrapped, not reimplemented.

# 2. Implementation

## 2.1 Architecture
tbanalyzer is a meta-pipeline built on the nf-core v4 template [@ewels2020nfcore] over Nextflow [@ditommaso2017nextflow], dispatching one of two sub-workflows from a shared samplesheet via a `--mode` flag. nf-core compatibility and a bundled reference set are implementation choices that support reproducibility and ease of use; they are not the contribution.

## 2.2 `--mode mtbseq`
Per-sample lineage classification and drug-resistance profiling, wrapping the MTBseq analysis [@kohl2018mtbseq] with parallelised per-sample orchestration.

## 2.3 `--mode magma`
Cohort joint-genotyping (GATK [@depristo2011gatk]) and structural-variant detection (DELLY [@rausch2012delly]), with resistance reporting, following the MAGMA methodology [@heupink2023magma]; MAGMA-mode internals are cited, not re-described, to keep the contribution distinct from the MAGMA 2.0 paper.

## 2.4 Shared infrastructure
Common FastQC + MultiQC quality control and software-version reporting span both modes, so the output structure is consistent regardless of analytical depth.

# 4. Discussion

[TODO — write against the validation.] tbanalyzer's value is *continuity*: the same cohort, the same inputs, two analytical depths. We discuss when to use which mode (routine surveillance vs research-depth re-analysis) and the pipeline's relationship to its upstreams (it wraps MTBseq and the MAGMA methodology; it does not modify their callers). **Anti-claims (must hold):** tbanalyzer is **not** an execution-infrastructure paper (that is the separate nf-nomad executor substrate); **not** a clinical certification; **not** a new variant caller (GATK/DELLY/LoFreq are the callers); and **not** a replacement for TB-Profiler — it serves a different analytical scope (cohort joint-genotyping + SV) alongside, not instead of, fast single-sample profiling. **Limitations:** no clinical certification; MAGMA-mode VQSR thresholds are defaults.
